# B2 Reference Architectures for Generative Video: full text

> Generated by tools/generate_catalog.py from the pages listed below; links are relative to the repository root. Product behavior is authoritative at https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning.

<!-- source: docs/gen-video.md -->

# Generative video on Backblaze B2 (agent-readable)

Catalog updated: 2026-11-16. The [Backblaze B2 documentation](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage) is the authority on current product behavior.

## Workload
Generative video produces more data per request than almost any other AI workload. Training corpora run from hundreds of TB to PB, checkpoints from tens of GB to TB, and every generation leaves behind keyframes, takes, variants, frame sequences and delivery renditions. Hosted model providers return result URLs that expire.

## Where does B2 fit?
B2 can be the durable system of record across that lifecycle:

- raw footage lake and versioned shard releases that training clusters in any GPU cloud stream from;
- checkpoint, LoRA and model-weight store that ComfyUI and Diffusers workers pull from;
- output sink and provenance-manifest store for hosted multi-provider generation, with Object Lock on a dedicated bucket where retention matters;
- review and approval stages driven by Event Notifications and legal hold;
- CDN origin, with no B2 download fees for egress to CDN partners.

Configure each integration with the B2 regional endpoint, bucket region, addressing style, and scoped credentials specified in its setup guide. Select a B2-specific provider preset where the integration offers one. For APIs that only ingest URLs, hand over a presigned URL; for a CDN, use the bucket as origin.

## Which architecture fits my use case?

| Use case | Architecture | Key integrations |
|---|---|---|
| Curate a text-to-video training corpus from licensed footage | [curate-video-training-corpus](architectures/curate-video-training-corpus/architecture.md) | rclone, video2dataset, Cosmos Curator, Daft, Pixeltable, LanceDB |
| Stream shards into training; version checkpoints and LoRAs | [stream-shards-train-video-diffusion](architectures/stream-shards-train-video-diffusion/architecture.md) | MosaicML Streaming, LitData, Ray Train, Composer, MLflow, ZenML, W&B |
| Self-hosted ComfyUI farm with shared weights and outputs | [self-hosted-video-diffusion-farm](architectures/self-hosted-video-diffusion-farm/architecture.md) | ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes, HF Cache Sync |
| Hosted multi-provider generation with provenance | [hosted-multi-provider-generation-provenance](architectures/hosted-multi-provider-generation-provenance/architecture.md) | Application workers, Runway API, Replicate |
| Moderate, review and approve before publishing | [moderate-review-approve-generated-video](architectures/moderate-review-approve-generated-video/architecture.md) | iconik, EditShare FLOW, B2 Event Notifications |
| Finish, transcode and deliver through a CDN | [finish-package-deliver-generated-video](architectures/finish-package-deliver-generated-video/architecture.md) | Cloudflare, bunny.net, Fastly, Telestream Vantage, Mux |

## B2 capabilities that apply
- **Access:** S3-compatible API, presigned URLs (provider handoff, review, Mux ingest), CORS for players, multipart upload for masters and checkpoints, and scoped application keys (one bucket, one optional prefix, and a capability list per key).
- **Change and lifecycle:** Event Notifications (signed webhooks, at-least-once delivery, enabled through Backblaze Support), and lifecycle rules that hide and then delete objects by prefix and age.
- **Protection:** Governance-mode default retention on raw footage and manifests, per-object retention on released weights, and legal hold on disputed assets. SSE-B2 is optional. Cloud Replication is bucket-to-bucket DR, not delivery.
- **Delivery:** server-side copy for stage promotion, `Cache-Control` from bucket info, and CDN-partner egress terms. See [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing).

## When Overdrive may apply
[B2 Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) may apply to sustained, high-throughput reads: multi-node diffusion training streaming shards, or GPU curation passes over PB of footage, where measurement shows object-store throughput rather than GPU decode is the bottleneck. Benchmark shard size and worker count against B2 first. Overdrive does not apply to hosted-API generation, moderation, or CDN-cached delivery.

## Where B2 does not fit
Keep these off object storage:

- job queues
- experiment-tracking, rights, MAM and billing databases
- in-RAM vector indexes
- node-local NVMe shard and weight caches
- GPU VRAM
- scratch frames during a render
- provider API keys and signing keys
- CDN edge caches

B2 is not a POSIX filesystem for in-place edits, and Cloud Replication is not a customer delivery mechanism.

## Provider output retention
Replicate deletes API outputs after one hour by default, so copy them to B2 within that window.

## Links
[README](README.md) - [Architecture index](docs/architecture-index.md) - [Related B2 samples](docs/related-b2-samples.md) - [B2 config examples](examples/README.md) - [B2 docs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage) - [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) - [Backblaze Labs](https://backblazelabs.com/) - [B2 samples](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples)

# Ingest licensed footage, then split, caption and curate a text-to-video training corpus

## Workload

Text-to-video and image-to-video teams turn licensed, partner and permissively licensed source footage into a training corpus. Scene detection cuts footage into clips; filters score aesthetics, motion, OCR text coverage, blur and safety; perceptual or embedding dedupe removes near-duplicates; VLMs and ASR write captions. Each corpus version must be traceable to the footage, recipe and run that produced it.

B2 is the system of record for raw footage and for every curated artifact. GPU compute in any cloud reads B2 over the S3 API; nothing requires copying the full corpus to each node.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SRC[On-prem disks / other clouds / URL lists] -->|rclone B2 backend<br/>video2dataset fsspec| RAW[(org-genvid-raw<br/>raw/source/<br/>Object Lock or versioning)]
  RIGHTS[(Rights and licence DB)] -.->|source IDs| RAW
  RAW -->|ranged GETs, read-only key| CUR[GPU curation<br/>Cosmos Curator / Daft / Pixeltable]
  CUR -->|split, score, filter, dedupe| CAP[VLM captions + faster-whisper ASR]
  CUR -->|scratch frames| SCRATCH[(org-genvid-curated<br/>scratch/run/<br/>lifecycle expiry)]
  CAP -->|clips, keyframes, captions, scores| CURATED[(org-genvid-curated<br/>curated/run_id/)]
  CUR -->|embeddings| LANCE[(org-genvid-curated<br/>index/clips.lance)]
  CURATED --> CARD[Dataset card + run stats + recipe]
  CARD --> TRAIN[Shard packing for training]
```

The [shard-streaming architecture](architectures/stream-shards-train-video-diffusion/architecture.md) picks up from the curated bucket.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-genvid-raw` | `raw/<source>/<batch>/` | Versioning on; no expiry while licensed | Enabled at creation, default governance retention set from licence terms | Immutable source footage with licence and consent sidecars (`<object>.license.json`) |
| `<org>-genvid-curated` | `curated/<run_id>/{clips,keyframes,captions,scores}/` | Keep; superseded runs expired only by explicit decision | Not enabled | Curated clips, keyframes, caption JSONL and score Parquet per run |
| `<org>-genvid-curated` | `index/<table>.lance/` | Keep | Not enabled | Lance clip-embedding table |
| `<org>-genvid-curated` | `runs/<run_id>/` | Keep | Not enabled | Recipe config, per-operator stats, dataset card |
| `<org>-genvid-curated` | `scratch/<run_id>/` | Lifecycle: hide after N days, delete after hide ([example](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | Not enabled | Intermediates that must not outlive the run |

Object Lock is a bucket property with per-object or bucket-default retention, not a prefix property, so raw footage gets its own bucket. Bucket names are globally unique; replace `<org>` and expect collisions.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| URL frontier and download-status queue | Postgres, Redis or Spark state | Transactional, high-churn updates |
| Rights and licence database | Relational database | Authoritative, queryable, access-controlled; B2 holds only sidecar copies |
| Ray or Slurm task state | Scheduler | Not durable data |
| GPU-local decode scratch | Node NVMe | Latency-sensitive random I/O |
| In-RAM FAISS index during dedupe | Worker memory | Rebuilt per run; the durable embeddings live in Lance on B2 |
| Run-tracking database | Relational database | Queries across runs; B2 holds the per-run artifacts |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How or why not |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | All tools reach B2 at `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the bucket region |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | No | No browser or third-party URL handoff in this workflow |
| Large-file multipart upload | Yes | Source masters and large shards; rclone and boto3-based tools handle it |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Ingest writer, curation reader, curated writer; see below |
| Event notifications | No | Curation runs are batch-scheduled; add notifications only if ingest should trigger runs |
| Object versions | Yes | Raw bucket, so overwrites and deletes are recoverable |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | `scratch/` only ([example](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)); B2 lifecycle hides, then deletes, by prefix and age |
| SSE | Optional | SSE-B2 default encryption if policy requires it |
| Object Lock | Yes | Raw bucket default governance retention ([example](examples/object-lock-governance.json)) |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | Bucket-to-bucket DR copy of raw footage; not a delivery path |
| Included egress / CDN / compute partners | Indirect | GPU clusters in other clouds read B2 directly; see [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for egress terms |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard | Standard B2 by default; [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) only if measured object throughput, not decode, limits runs; node NVMe holds per-task scratch only |

## Integration configuration

All endpoints use `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from `B2_REGION`. Never hardcode a region.

- **rclone (built-in B2 backend).** Configure a `b2` remote with an application key restricted to `<org>-genvid-raw` and `raw/`, `writeFiles` plus `listFiles`. rclone's [B2 backend docs](https://rclone.org/b2/) describe this. Use it for bulk seeding from disks and other clouds.
- **video2dataset (fsspec / s3fs).** Set the output folder to `s3://<org>-genvid-raw/raw/<source>/` and configure fsspec with `endpoint_url` under `s3.client_kwargs` as the B2 endpoint, as the README shows.
- **NVIDIA Cosmos Curator (S3 custom endpoint).** Configure `region` and `endpoint_url` in `~/.aws/credentials`, which is the only file Cosmos Curator reads ([end-user guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-curator/blob/main/docs/client/end-user-guide.md)). Mount that file from a secret; give it the curation-reader profile for raw input and a separate curated-writer profile for output where the pipeline allows two profiles.
- **Daft (S3 custom endpoint).** `IOConfig(s3=S3Config(endpoint_url=..., key_id=..., access_key=..., region_name=...))` per the [config API docs](https://docs.daft.ai/en/stable/api/config/).
- **Pixeltable (built-in B2 option).** Add a `[b2]` profile with the application key to `~/.aws/credentials`, set `b2_profile = "b2"` in `config.toml`, and point media destinations at `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<bucket>/<prefix>/` ([Backblaze B2 section](https://docs.pixeltable.com/integrations/cloud-storage)).
- **LanceDB / Lance (S3 custom endpoint).** Use the [pinned connection profile](examples/lancedb.md) for clip embeddings in the curated bucket. It specifies the B2 endpoint, region, credentials and a Lance version whose S3 commit handler requires one writer per table. Serialize ingest, index creation, compaction and other mutations through one writer service; readers can run separately. Endpoint settings alone do not establish safe commit behavior across Lance versions.

Other curation tools that read `s3://` paths work the same way once their S3 client points at the B2 endpoint. For Ray Data `read_videos`, pass a `pyarrow.fs.S3FileSystem(endpoint_override=...)` as `filesystem` ([API reference](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/data/api/doc/ray.data.read_videos.html)). For Data-Juicer, the [Data-Juicer sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/data-juicer-multimodal-curation) handles B2 I/O in its app layer.

## Security

| Role | Bucket / prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| ingest-writer | `<org>-genvid-raw` / `raw/` | `listFiles,writeFiles` |
| curation-reader | `<org>-genvid-raw` / `raw/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| curated-writer | `<org>-genvid-curated` / (whole bucket, or `curated/` + a separate `scratch/` key) | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles` |
| takedown-admin | `<org>-genvid-raw` (whole bucket) | `listFiles,readFiles,deleteFiles,bypassGovernance`; audited break-glass use only |
| provisioning (admin) | account | Bucket, lifecycle and retention setup only; never in runtime |

A key scopes to one bucket, one optional prefix and a capability list ([keys docs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)). Secrets go in a gitignored `0600` `.env` or the cluster secret store; never in recipes, notebooks or logs. Governance retention lets a privileged key override a lock; choose compliance mode only for a contractual requirement because it cannot be shortened.

## Takedown and erasure

Licences get revoked, rights holders send takedown notices, and people withdraw consent (for example a GDPR erasure request). Retention on the raw bucket must not make those deletions impossible.

- **Governance mode (this repo's default).** Deleting a locked version early needs `bypassGovernance` together with `deleteFiles`. No runtime role holds them. Use a dedicated `takedown-admin` key, kept out of pipelines, used only from an audited process that records the request, the object versions deleted and the approver.
- **Compliance mode.** No key can delete a locked version before its retention ends, and retention cannot be shortened. Do not use it for footage that contains personal data or depends on revocable licences.
- **Downstream copies.** Deleting raw footage does not remove the clips, captions, embeddings and shards built from it. The run ID and source IDs in each dataset card identify affected `curated/<run_id>/` objects and Lance rows. Rebuild or filter the next dataset version, and record the takedown in the dataset card.
- **Published outputs.** Takedowns of generated or published assets follow the legal-hold and audit process in the [moderation architecture](architectures/moderate-review-approve-generated-video/architecture.md).

- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)

<!-- source: architectures/stream-shards-train-video-diffusion/architecture.md -->

# Stream video shards into distributed diffusion training and version checkpoints and LoRAs

## Workload

Video diffusion transformers train on curated clips or on precomputed VAE latents and text embeddings. Training spans many GPUs, often across neocloud providers, and is preempted. Each run emits periodic multi-GB checkpoints, LoRA adapters, sample clips and eval metrics. Released weights must trace back to a dataset version and run.

B2 holds versioned shards, checkpoints, artifacts and promoted weights. It is reachable from every cluster through one S3 endpoint, so moving compute does not mean moving data.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CUR[(org-genvid-curated<br/>curated/run_id/)] -->|pack| SH[(org-genvid-datasets<br/>datasets/name/version/shards/)]
  SH -->|ranged GETs, read-only key| NVME[Node NVMe shard cache]
  NVME --> TRAIN[Multi-node training<br/>Streaming / LitData / WebDataset]
  TRAIN -->|save_folder / storage_path| CK[(org-genvid-training<br/>checkpoints/run_id/step_n/<br/>lifecycle by age)]
  TRAIN -->|samples, metrics, LoRAs| TRK[MLflow / ZenML / W&B]
  TRK -->|artifact store / reference| ART[(org-genvid-training<br/>artifacts/run_id/)]
  CK -->|on approval: publisher downloads<br/>with promotion-reader, re-uploads| MOD[(org-genvid-models<br/>models/name/version/<br/>loras/subject/version/)]
  MOD --> INF[Inference workers]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant J as Training job
  participant B as B2 (checkpoints/)
  participant S as Scheduler
  J->>B: multipart upload step_n
  S-->>J: preempt
  S->>J: restart on another cluster
  J->>B: list checkpoints/run_id/, read latest step
  J->>J: resume from step_n
```

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-genvid-datasets` | `datasets/<name>/<version>/shards/` + `index.json` | New version = new prefix; never rewritten | Optional | WebDataset tars, MDS or LitData chunks |
| `<org>-genvid-training` | `checkpoints/<run_id>/step_<n>/` | Lifecycle: hide after N days, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-checkpoints.json)) | Not enabled | Resumable checkpoints |
| `<org>-genvid-training` | `artifacts/<run_id>/` | Keep | Not enabled | MLflow artifacts, sample MP4 grids, eval metrics |
| `<org>-genvid-models` | `models/<name>/<version>/`, `loras/<subject>/<version>/` | Keep | Per-object governance retention for released weights; no bucket default | Promoted weights read by inference |

B2 lifecycle rules act on prefix and age (`daysFromUploadingToHiding`, `daysFromHidingToDeleting`); they cannot keep the last K checkpoints. Promote keepers to `models/` (download and re-upload, see Security) before the expiry window, or exclude a run by giving it a prefix with no rule.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Shard cache and shuffle buffers | Node NVMe / RAM | Random access during an epoch |
| In-memory checkpoint staging, NCCL state | GPU host memory | Transient |
| Experiment-tracking backend DB | MLflow / ZenML / W&B backend | Queryable metadata; bytes go to B2 |
| Scheduler and job queue | Slurm, Kubernetes, Ray | Control plane |
| Dataset registry DB | Relational DB | Maps versions to runs; points at B2 prefixes |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How or why not |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Concurrent ranged GETs from many workers |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | No | All access is server-side with keys |
| Large-file multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB checkpoints and shards |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Read-only shard key, checkpoint writer, publisher |
| Event notifications | No | Promotion is an explicit pipeline step |
| Object versions | Default | B2 keeps prior versions of any rewritten key; versioned prefixes avoid rewrites, and the models bucket keeps versions for Object Lock |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Age-based expiry on `checkpoints/` |
| Server-side copy | No | Checkpoints and released weights live in different buckets, and a [CopyObject](https://www.backblaze.com/apidocs/s3-copy-object) runs under one key that must read the source and write the destination; promotion downloads and re-uploads instead |
| SSE | Optional | SSE-B2 default encryption |
| Object Lock | Optional | Separate models bucket for released weights ([example](examples/object-lock-governance.json)) |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | DR copy of the models bucket |
| Included egress / compute partners | Yes | Training clusters in other clouds read B2 directly; see [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard + NVMe cache | Benchmark shard size and worker count against B2 first (the [WebDataset streaming sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training) reports live throughput); consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) when sustained multi-node read throughput is the measured bottleneck |

## Integration configuration

Endpoint everywhere: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from `B2_REGION`.

- **MosaicML Streaming (built-in B2 option).** Set `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` to the B2 endpoint and the application key as `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`; the [cloud-credential guide](https://docs.mosaicml.com/projects/streaming/en/stable/how_to_guides/configure_cloud_storage_credentials.html) gives the Backblaze template. Use `remote=s3://<org>-genvid-datasets/datasets/<name>/<version>/` and a node-local `local` cache.
- **Lightning LitData (S3 custom endpoint).** Pass `storage_options={"S3_ENDPOINT_URL": ...}` (or the boto3 `endpoint_url`) to both `optimize` and `StreamingDataset` ([README](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/litData)).
- **Ray Train (built-in B2 option).** Set `storage_path="s3://<org>-genvid-training/checkpoints?endpoint_override=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com"`, or set `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` with the application key in `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, as the Backblaze B2 section of the [persistent-storage guide](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html) shows.
- **Composer (S3 custom endpoint).** Set `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` to the B2 endpoint and `save_folder="s3://<org>-genvid-training/checkpoints/<run_id>"`; Composer writes locally, then uploads, and `load_path` resumes from remote ([checkpointing docs](https://docs.mosaicml.com/projects/composer/en/stable/trainer/checkpointing.html)).
- **MLflow (built-in B2 option).** Set the artifact root to `b2://<bucket>@s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<path>` with the application key in `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` set to the bucket region ([artifact-store docs](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/)). Use an application key, not the master key. `s3://` with `MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` also works.
- **ZenML (built-in B2 option).** Run `zenml integration install b2` and register an artifact store with `--flavor=b2`, `--path=s3://<org>-genvid-training/artifacts/` and `endpoint_url` for the bucket region in `client_kwargs` ([ZenML B2 artifact store](https://docs.zenml.io/stacks/stack-components/artifact-stores/b2), [Backblaze guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-use-backblaze-b2-as-an-artifact-store-with-zenml)). Credentials come from `B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID` / `B2_APPLICATION_KEY` or a ZenML secret; scope the key to that prefix.
- **W&B reference artifacts (built-in B2 option).** Set `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` to the B2 endpoint and log `s3://` references to shards and checkpoints so W&B tracks them without copying bytes ([track external files](https://docs.coreweave.com/guides/artifacts/track-external-files/)).

Open-Sora, Wan, HunyuanVideo, FastVideo and finetrainers train from local paths: feed them through the streaming loaders above, or stage data and pull checkpoints with rclone.

## Security

| Role | Bucket / prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| shard-packer | `<org>-genvid-datasets` / `datasets/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| trainer-reader | `<org>-genvid-datasets` / `datasets/<name>/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| checkpoint-writer | `<org>-genvid-training` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles` |
| promotion-reader | `<org>-genvid-training` / `checkpoints/` | `listFiles,readFiles` (held by the publisher) |
| model-publisher | `<org>-genvid-models` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,writeFileRetentions` |
| inference-reader | `<org>-genvid-models` / `models/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |

Inject keys through the cluster secret store; never in job specs, logged configs or W&B run config. Promotion crosses buckets: the publisher downloads with the read-only `promotion-reader` key and re-uploads with `model-publisher`, verifying size and checksum after upload. Released weights use per-object retention in the models bucket. Enabling Object Lock alone does not retain objects; leave cached weights without retention and keep checkpoint pruning independent of release retention. Do not hand the publisher an unrestricted key for convenience.

## References

- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 large files](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-large-files)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [B2 Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive)
- Samples: [WebDataset Streaming PyTorch Training](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training), [LoRA Training Studio](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lora-training-studio)

<!-- source: architectures/self-hosted-video-diffusion-farm/architecture.md -->

# Run a self-hosted open-weight video diffusion farm with shared weights and outputs

## Workload

A studio or platform runs open-weight video models (for example Wan, HunyuanVideo, LTX-Video) in ComfyUI on GPU instances that start and stop with demand, often across several GPU clouds. Each worker needs the same multi-GB checkpoints, VAEs, text encoders and LoRAs. Each job produces MP4 or WebM output that must outlive the worker and be shareable for review.

B2 is the shared model store and the durable output store. Worker NVMe is a cache, not a source of truth.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  HUB[Hugging Face Hub] -->|hf-cache-sync push| HF[(org-genvid-models<br/>models/hf-cache/)]
  TEAM[Custom checkpoints / LoRAs] --> MD[(org-genvid-models<br/>models/family/version/)]
  HF -->|pull on cold start| W[ComfyUI worker<br/>NVMe cache]
  MD -->|Download Model from Cloud<br/>skip if ETag matches| W
  WF[(org-genvid-renders<br/>workflows/ + inputs/)] --> W
  Q[Job queue] --> W
  W -->|Save Video to Cloud<br/>+ workflow JSON + seed| R[(org-genvid-renders<br/>renders/tenant/date/job_id/)]
  W -->|frames, checkpointed jobs only| S[(org-genvid-renders<br/>scratch/job/<br/>lifecycle expiry)]
  R -->|presigned GET| REV[Reviewer]
```

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-genvid-models` | `models/hf-cache/` | Keep (content-addressed blobs and revision refs) | No retention applied | Mirrored Hugging Face cache |
| `<org>-genvid-models` | `models/<family>/<version>/` | Keep; new version = new prefix | Per-version retention when released | Custom checkpoints, VAEs, LoRAs with licence files |
| `<org>-genvid-renders` | `workflows/<name>/<version>.json`, `inputs/<tenant>/` | Keep | Not enabled | Versioned ComfyUI graphs and reference inputs |
| `<org>-genvid-renders` | `renders/<tenant>/<date>/<job_id>/` | Keep (or expire per tenant policy) | Not enabled | Output video, workflow JSON, seed |
| `<org>-genvid-renders` | `scratch/<job_id>/` | Lifecycle: hide, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | Not enabled | Intermediate frames |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Hot weights | GPU VRAM and worker NVMe | Load latency; B2 is the cache's source |
| Job queue | Redis, SQS or Temporal | Transactional dispatch |
| User, session and billing DB | Relational DB | Application state |
| Scratch frames during a render | Worker disk | High-churn random I/O; only persisted to `scratch/` when a job is checkpointed |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How or why not |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Nodes and hf-cache-sync use the S3 endpoint |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Time-limited GET links for reviewers |
| CORS | Optional | Only if a browser app fetches renders with JavaScript ([example](examples/cors-playback.json)) |
| Large-file multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB checkpoints pushed to `models/` |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Read-only models key on workers; write key on renders |
| ETag on HEAD | Yes | Download node skips files whose local ETag matches; multipart ETags are not MD5s, so compare ETag to ETag, not to a local hash |
| Event notifications | No | Outputs are returned synchronously to the job |
| Object versions | Default | B2 keeps prior versions by default; versioned prefixes avoid rewrites, and a keep-latest rule ([example](examples/lifecycle-keep-latest.json)) cleans up any prefix whose keys are rewritten |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | `scratch/` expiry |
| SSE | Optional | SSE-B2 default encryption |
| Object Lock / replication | Optional (released weights) | Lock a dedicated bucket for released custom weights if retention must be provable; upstream weights are reproducible, so add replication for DR only if they are not |
| Included egress / CDN | Indirect | Workers in other clouds pull weights; see [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard + NVMe cache | ETag-validated NVMe cache absorbs repeats; Overdrive only if a large fleet cold-starts at once and measured throughput limits it |

## Integration configuration

- **ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes (built-in B2 option).** Set `COMFY_S3_PROVIDER` to the Backblaze B2 preset and `COMFY_S3_REGION` to the bucket region; `COMFY_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` overrides the derived endpoint. Nodes cover Save Video to Cloud, image and audio input loading (there is no video load node), ETag-cached model download and presigned share URLs ([README](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage)). Give the worker two keys if the node supports it (read-only models, write renders); otherwise run the worker with the renders key and pre-pull models with a read-only key in an init step.
- **HF Cache Sync (built-in B2 option).** Set `B2_ENDPOINT`, `B2_BUCKET`, `B2_REGION`, `B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID` and `B2_APPLICATION_KEY`, or the `storage.*` keys in `.hf-cache-sync.yaml`; `hf-cache-sync doctor` reports which source it used ([README](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/hf-cache-sync)). A CI job with a write key pushes; workers and CI pull with a read-only key.

Endpoint: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the bucket region.

## Security

| Role | Bucket / prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| model-publisher (CI) | `<org>-genvid-models` / `models/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| worker-model-reader | `<org>-genvid-models` / `models/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| worker-render-writer | `<org>-genvid-renders` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| share-signer | `<org>-genvid-renders` / `renders/` | `readFiles` |

Presigned URLs are bearer credentials; keep expiry short. Custom ComfyUI nodes run with whatever credentials are in the worker environment, so review third-party nodes before installing them. Respect each open-weight model's licence for hosted use and keep it next to the weights.

## References

- [B2 S3 presigned URLs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)
- Samples: [ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage), [HF Cache Sync](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/hf-cache-sync), [Awesome Video Generation](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/awesome-video-generation)

<!-- source: architectures/hosted-multi-provider-generation-provenance/architecture.md -->

# Generate video across hosted model APIs and keep every output with a provenance manifest

## Workload

A product turns a prompt into a short video. It writes a storyboard, generates keyframe images, fans those out to hosted image-to-video or text-to-video models (Runway, Replicate-hosted models, Kling or Wan through GMICloud, NVIDIA Cosmos), adds TTS narration and music, and composes the result with ffmpeg. Providers return result URLs that expire, and each generation is billed. Teams compare providers, re-run or fork promising runs, and answer disclosure and takedown requests.

B2 is the provider-neutral record. Application workers copy every intermediate and final asset into B2 as soon as the provider returns it, alongside a manifest that records what produced it. A separate writer copies approved manifests into the Object Lock bucket when retention is required.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[Prompt] --> G[Application / orchestration workers]
  IN[(org-genvid-runs<br/>inputs/tenant/)] -->|presigned GET, or app relay<br/>to Runway upload API| PROV[Hosted providers<br/>Runway / Replicate / GMICloud / Cosmos]
  G --> PROV
  PROV -->|expiring result URL| G
  G -->|sink: copy immediately| RUN[(org-genvid-runs<br/>runs/tenant/date/run_id/)]
  G -->|completed manifest| AUD[Audit publisher<br/>separate manifest credential]
  AUD -->|SHA-256, provider, model,<br/>prompt, params, seed, parent_run_id| MAN[(org-genvid-manifests<br/>Object Lock bucket)]
  RUN --> FF[ffmpeg compose]
  FF --> RUN
  RUN -->|presigned GET| REV[Review / compare]
  MAN -->|replay or fork| G
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant B2
  participant Prov as Provider API
  App->>B2: PUT inputs/... (explicit Content-Type)
  alt Runway
    App->>B2: GET input (scoped read key)
    App->>Prov: POST /v1/uploads, then upload file
    Prov-->>App: runway:// URI (valid 24 h)
  else URL-ingest provider (Replicate)
    App->>B2: presign GET (short expiry)
  end
  App->>Prov: create task with input URI or URL
  Prov-->>App: result URL (expires; Replicate: 1 h default)
  App->>Prov: GET result within the retention window
  App->>B2: PUT runs/.../output.mp4
  App->>B2: PUT manifest last
```

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-genvid-runs` | `inputs/<tenant>/<sha256>.<ext>` | Lifecycle expiry after the provider fetch window if inputs are not needed | Not enabled | Reference images and clips handed to providers |
| `<org>-genvid-runs` | `runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/` or content-addressed `sha256/<hash>` | Keep | Not enabled | Keyframes, takes, audio, composed output |
| `<org>-genvid-manifests` | `manifests/<tenant>/<run_id>.json` | Keep | Enabled at creation; default governance retention; legal hold for disputes ([example](examples/object-lock-governance.json)) | Retained-unchanged run manifests |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Provider API keys | Secrets manager | Credentials |
| Job queue | Queue service | Dispatch and retries |
| User, tenant and billing DB | Relational DB | Application state |
| Search index over manifest metadata | Search DB | Query; B2 holds source manifests |
| C2PA or manifest signing keys | KMS or HSM | Signing keys never touch object storage |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How or why not |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Application workers persist outputs and manifests through an S3 client |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Provider input handoff and reviewer access |
| CORS | Optional | Only for a browser review UI ([example](examples/cors-playback.json)) |
| Multipart upload | Rarely | Clips are usually small; the SDK handles it if needed |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Bucket-restricted read/write for the pipeline; separate manifest writer |
| Event notifications | No | Here; the [moderation architecture](architectures/moderate-review-approve-generated-video/architecture.md) adds them |
| Object versions | Via Object Lock | Lock-enabled buckets keep versions |
| Lifecycle rules | Optional | Expire `inputs/` after use |
| SSE | Optional | SSE-B2 default encryption |
| Object Lock and legal hold | Yes | Manifest bucket only |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | DR copy of manifests; not delivery |
| CDN / Overdrive | No | Throughput is bounded by provider latency, not storage |

## Integration configuration

- **Application workers.** Use an S3 client configured with the B2 endpoint, region and scoped application key. Stream provider outputs into B2, compute SHA-256 over the stored content, and write the manifest after all required assets are complete.
- **Runway API (application relay).** The app reads the input from B2 with a scoped read key and sends it to Runway's [ephemeral upload API](https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/assets/uploads/) (`POST /v1/uploads`, 512 bytes to 200 MB), which returns a `runway://` URI valid for 24 hours; use that URI in the generation request. Runway's [URL inputs](https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/assets/inputs/) must answer HEAD without redirect and return `Content-Length` and a specific `Content-Type`. A SigV4 presigned URL is signed for one HTTP method, so use the upload API, or a public or CDN-fronted URL, rather than a GET-presigned URL. Copy completed results into B2 before their provider URLs expire.
- **Replicate (URL ingest).** [Input files](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files) can be hosted URLs, so pass a B2 presigned GET. Per [data retention](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/data-retention), API prediction inputs, outputs and output files are deleted after one hour by default, so the sink must copy outputs into B2 within that window. Retry the copy from the job queue, not from a later user request.

Other hosted providers follow the same persistence pattern. Use presigned GET inputs where the provider supports them; otherwise relay bytes through its upload API. For fal.ai, input parameters vary by model and outputs use public expiring URLs, so copy results into B2 in the completion worker.

### Optional implementation example: Genblaze

[Genblaze](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze) is one SDK option for the application worker. Follow its [installation and pipeline examples](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze#storage). Configure the storage sink as follows, with `B2_BUCKET` set to the private runs bucket and `B2_REGION`, `B2_KEY_ID` and `B2_APP_KEY` supplied by the service environment:

```python
import os
from genblaze_core import KeyStrategy, ObjectStorageSink
from genblaze_s3 import S3StorageBackend

storage = ObjectStorageSink(
    S3StorageBackend.for_backblaze(os.environ["B2_BUCKET"]),
    prefix="",
    key_strategy=KeyStrategy.HIERARCHICAL,
)
# Pass this sink to the configured pipeline: pipeline.run(sink=storage).
```

Set the run's `tenant_id` from authenticated application context. The empty root prefix and hierarchical strategy produce `runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/` rather than the SDK's default content-addressed layout. Keep `listBuckets` on this bucket-restricted key for the backend's `HeadBucket` preflight. The sink writes assets and the run manifest to the same runs bucket; the audit publisher must copy the approved manifest to `manifests/<tenant>/<run_id>.json` using the separate manifest-bucket credential.

## Provenance

The manifest records per-asset SHA-256, provider, model and version, prompt, parameters, seed, timestamps and `parent_run_id`. Write it last as the run's completion marker. Sign the manifest with a KMS-held key or C2PA Content Credentials to establish its authenticity. Object Lock preserves the retained object version; record the approved manifest's version ID or trusted digest so readers resolve that approved content even if a writer uploads a new version under the same key.

Keep `runs/` private. Record bucket, key, version ID where available, and `sha256` as durable asset references; issue presigned URLs at read time. A raw object URL does not grant access to a private bucket. This also applies to the optional Genblaze sink: URL-based verification needs an authorized fetch path, while the persisted provenance record should not contain expiring bearer URLs.

## Security

| Role | Bucket / prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| pipeline-writer | `<org>-genvid-runs` | `listBuckets,listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` (`HeadBucket` preflight and input reads for the Runway upload relay) |
| input-signer | `<org>-genvid-runs` / `inputs/` | `readFiles` |
| manifest-writer | `<org>-genvid-manifests` / `manifests/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` (no `writeFileRetentions` or `bypassGovernance`) |
| legal-hold-admin | `<org>-genvid-manifests` | `writeFileLegalHolds,readFileLegalHolds` |

Keep provider API keys out of manifests and logs. Presigned input URLs expire after the provider's fetch window.

## References

- [Genblaze developer guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-genblaze-developer-guide)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [C2PA specification](https://c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.1/index.html)
- Samples: [Genblaze SDK](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze), [Genblaze x GMICloud](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze-gmicloud-pipeline), [multi-provider gen-media sample](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze-gen-media-multi-provider-sample), [NVIDIA Nemotron x Genblaze](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/nvidia-nemotron-genblaze-b2), [AI Avatar Video Generator](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/ai-avatar-video-generator), [Comic Storyboard](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/comic-storyboard-b2)

<!-- source: architectures/moderate-review-approve-generated-video/architecture.md -->

# Moderate, review and approve generated video before it is published

## Workload

Generated clips have to pass policy, brand and legal checks before release. Automated classification catches clear violations, a hash check confirms the asset matches its generation manifest, and editors review the rest in a media asset manager (MAM). Disputed assets must be preserved unchanged. Copying assets between moderation tools, a MAM and an archive creates divergent copies and breaks the audit trail.

B2 holds one copy per stage. The stage is expressed as a prefix in a single Object Lock-enabled bucket, so moderation, MAM and publishing all point at the same objects. Pre-approval stages sit under `inbox/` so one prefix-scoped key can cover them without reaching `published/`.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  GEN[Generators] -->|PUT| ST[(org-genvid-review<br/>inbox/staging/tenant/asset_id/)]
  ST -->|B2 Event Notification<br/>signed webhook| EB[b2-event-broker]
  EB --> MOD[Moderation worker<br/>frame sampling + classifier]
  EB --> VER[Manifest verifier<br/>recompute SHA-256]
  MOD -->|report| MR[(inbox/moderation/asset_id/)]
  MOD -->|violation: copy then delete| Q[(inbox/quarantine/asset_id/)]
  VER -->|mismatch| Q
  ST -->|bucket scan, proxies| MAM[iconik / EditShare FLOW]
  MAM -->|approve| PUB[Publisher]
  PUB -->|server-side copy,<br/>then hide staging| P[(published/asset_id/)]
  PUB -->|dispute| LH[Legal hold on object version]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant B2
  participant Broker as Event broker
  participant Mod as Moderation
  B2->>Broker: POST event (X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature)
  Broker->>Broker: verify HMAC, dedupe by event ID
  Broker-->>B2: 200 quickly
  Broker->>Mod: enqueue asset_id
  Mod->>B2: GET staging object (ranged frames)
  Mod->>B2: PUT moderation report
```

## B2 zones

One bucket, `<org>-genvid-review`, created with Object Lock enabled and **no default retention**, so normal stage transitions can delete. Legal hold is applied per object version when needed.

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-genvid-review` | `inbox/staging/<tenant>/<asset_id>/` | Lifecycle: delete hidden versions 7 days after hiding; current objects are never hidden by age ([example](examples/lifecycle-staging-hidden.json)) | Legal hold on dispute | New generations awaiting checks |
| `<org>-genvid-review` | `inbox/moderation/<asset_id>/` | Keep | Optional retention per object | Classifier reports and flagged crops |
| `<org>-genvid-review` | `inbox/quarantine/<asset_id>/` | Keep until case closed | Legal hold when disputed | Flagged assets; never reachable from CDN |
| `<org>-genvid-review` | `published/<asset_id>/` | Keep | Optional retention | Approved masters handed to [finishing and delivery](architectures/finish-package-deliver-generated-video/architecture.md) |

S3 has no move: quarantine is a server-side copy followed by a delete of the staging object, and promotion is a server-side copy followed by hiding the staging object. A legal hold blocks deleting the held version, so apply holds after the copy. Do not reuse the age-based `scratch/` rule here: it would hide and delete assets still waiting for review.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Moderation review queue and reviewer DB | Queue + relational DB | Workflow state |
| MAM metadata DBs | iconik / FLOW | The MAM indexes B2 objects; it does not replace them |
| Takedown ticketing | Ticketing system | Case management |
| Signing keys | KMS or HSM | Credentials |
| Event broker subscriber registry | Broker config store | Control plane |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How or why not |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Workers and publisher |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Reviewer access outside the MAM |
| CORS | No | Unless a custom review UI fetches media |
| Multipart upload | As needed | Long masters |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | One per stage role; see below |
| Event notifications | Yes | `b2:ObjectCreated:*` on `inbox/staging/` ([example](examples/event-notifications-staging.json)); enabled by Backblaze Support on request; at-least-once, signed ([reference guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide)) |
| Object versions | Yes | Implied by Object Lock |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Delete hidden `inbox/staging/` versions only ([example](examples/lifecycle-staging-hidden.json)) |
| SSE | Optional | SSE-B2 |
| Object Lock and legal hold | Yes | Legal hold on disputed versions |
| Server-side copy | Yes | Staging to published or quarantine |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | DR only |
| CDN / Overdrive | No | Delivery is the next architecture |

## Integration configuration

- **iconik (Backblaze guide).** Add a storage of type "Backblaze B2" with key ID, application key, bucket name, bucket ID and path. Enable Scan to build proxies ([guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-iconik-with-backblaze-b2)). This uses B2 key ID and bucket ID rather than an S3 endpoint. A B2 key allows one prefix, so add one iconik storage per stage: `inbox/staging/` with `mam-staging-reader`, and `published/` with `mam-published-reader` if editors work there. A single whole-bucket read-only key is simpler but also exposes `inbox/quarantine/`.
- **EditShare FLOW (Backblaze guide).** Add a "Backblaze" storage with key ID, application key and bucket name ([guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-editshare-flow-with-backblaze-b2)).
- **Event Notifications (B2 feature).** Configure rules with the native API ([`b2_set_bucket_notification_rules`](https://www.backblaze.com/apidocs/b2-set-bucket-notification-rules)); verify `X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature`, acknowledge fast, and dedupe because delivery is at-least-once ([overview](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications), [reference guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide)). The [B2 Event Broker sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker) implements verify-and-fan-out on Cloudflare Workers.

For Frame.io, run the [Frame.io custom action sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/backblaze-frameio), a bridge container that exports and imports assets between Frame.io and B2.

## Security

| Role | Bucket / prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| generator-writer | `<org>-genvid-review` / `inbox/staging/` | `writeFiles` |
| moderator | `<org>-genvid-review` / `inbox/` (reads staging, writes moderation and quarantine; cannot reach `published/`) | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles` |
| mam-staging-reader | `<org>-genvid-review` / `inbox/staging/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| mam-published-reader | `<org>-genvid-review` / `published/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| publisher | `<org>-genvid-review` (whole bucket: copy needs source and destination under one key) | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` (hiding staging needs only `writeFiles`; no `deleteFiles`) |
| legal-hold-admin | `<org>-genvid-review` | `readFileLegalHolds,writeFileLegalHolds` |

Release legal holds only through an audited process. Takedown and erasure requests that start in the [curation architecture](architectures/curate-video-training-corpus/architecture.md#takedown-and-erasure) follow the same audited path. Keep `inbox/quarantine/` private; no CDN or public path may reach this bucket.

## References

- [B2 Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications), [reference guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide) and [`b2_set_bucket_notification_rules`](https://www.backblaze.com/apidocs/b2-set-bucket-notification-rules)
- [`b2_hide_file`](https://www.backblaze.com/apidocs/b2-hide-file) (requires `writeFiles`)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)
- Samples: [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker), [NudeNet Video Moderation](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/nudenet-video-moderation), [Genblaze SDK](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze) (manifests to verify against), [Frame.io custom action](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/backblaze-frameio)

<!-- source: architectures/finish-package-deliver-generated-video/architecture.md -->

# Finish, transcode and deliver generated video through a CDN

## Workload

Many gen-video models emit short, low-resolution, low-frame-rate clips. Approved masters go through finishing passes: upscaling (Real-ESRGAN), frame interpolation (RIFE), matting (RobustVideoMatting), captions (Whisper) and per-platform cutdowns such as 9:16 shorts. Each master then fans out into an HLS ladder, posters, thumbnail sprites and WebVTT. Read traffic is heavy and repeated, so egress and duplicate copies drive cost.

B2 keeps masters, finishing outputs and delivery renditions in one place, and serves as the origin for a CDN partner. Managed video platforms fetch masters from B2 rather than becoming a second system of record.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  APP[(org-genvid-review<br/>published/asset_id/)] --> FIN[Finishing workers<br/>upscale / RIFE / matting / captions]
  FIN -->|frames| SC[(org-genvid-delivery<br/>scratch/job/<br/>lifecycle)]
  FIN -->|outputs + job manifest| RN[(org-genvid-delivery<br/>renders/job/)]
  RN --> TX[Transcode<br/>ffmpeg / Telestream Vantage]
  TX --> DL[(org-genvid-delivery<br/>delivery/asset_id/hls/)]
  DL -->|origin| CDN[Cloudflare / Fastly / bunny.net]
  CDN --> V[Viewers]
  RN -->|presigned GET| MUX[Mux ingest]
  MUX --> V
```

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-genvid-delivery` | `scratch/<job>/` | Lifecycle: hide, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | Not enabled | Finishing frames |
| `<org>-genvid-delivery` | `renders/<job>/` + `job.json` | Keep finished masters; expire superseded intermediates | Not enabled | Upscaled, interpolated, matted, captioned masters and cutdowns |
| `<org>-genvid-delivery` | `delivery/<asset_id>/hls/<rendition>/`, `posters/`, `sprites/`, `captions/` | Keep latest version only ([example](examples/lifecycle-keep-latest.json)) | Not enabled | CDN-served renditions |

A private bucket behind a signing edge app is the default. A public bucket is simpler, but every object in it becomes readable by URL. If you choose public, put only `delivery/` content in it, as a separate `<org>-genvid-public` bucket. Set `Cache-Control` through bucket info ([example](examples/bucket-info-cache-control.json)).

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CDN edge cache | CDN | Hot reads |
| Player analytics | Analytics service | Event data |
| Entitlement and auth | Auth service | Decides who gets a token |
| Finishing and transcode job queue | Queue | Dispatch |
| Mux-hosted renditions | Mux | When Mux handles playback, B2 keeps the master only |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How or why not |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Workers, Vantage, CDN origin |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Mux ingest; private review |
| CORS | Yes, if players fetch cross-origin | HLS players need it ([example](examples/cors-playback.json)) |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Long masters |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Finishing writer, transcoder, edge signer |
| Event notifications | Optional | Trigger transcode on `renders/` upload |
| Object versions | Default | B2 keeps prior versions by default, so rewritten playlists, posters and re-renders pile up as billed storage; add a keep-latest rule ([example](examples/lifecycle-keep-latest.json)) |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | `scratch/`, intermediates and keep-latest on `delivery/`; merge all rules for the bucket into one array before applying |
| SSE | Optional | SSE-B2 is transparent to signed edge reads |
| Object Lock / replication | No | Masters are retained upstream in the review bucket; add replication for DR if needed |
| Included egress / CDN partners | Yes | Backblaze does not charge download fees for egress to CDN partners such as Cloudflare, Fastly and bunny.net; see [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard + CDN | The CDN absorbs hot reads; Overdrive does not apply to edge-cached delivery |

## Integration configuration

Origin host: `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the bucket region.

- **Cloudflare (Backblaze guide).** Use a public bucket as origin, or a Worker that signs requests to a private bucket with a read-only key scoped to `delivery/` ([guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-deliver-private-backblaze-b2-content-through-cloudflare-cdn); sample: [cloudflare-b2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2)).
- **bunny.net (Backblaze guide).** The pull-zone origin is the B2 S3 endpoint. Enable S3 Authentication with the key ID and application key for private buckets ([guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-bunnynet-with-backblaze-b2)).
- **Fastly (Backblaze guide).** The B2 S3 endpoint is the origin, and a Compute app signs private reads ([guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-fastly-cdn-with-backblaze-b2); sample: [fastly-b2-rust](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/fastly-b2-rust)).
- **Telestream Vantage Gateway (Backblaze guide).** For source and destination, choose the NETAPP option and enter the B2 key ID, application key, S3 endpoint URL and bucket/path ([guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-vantage-gateway-with-backblaze-b2)).
- **Mux (presigned URL ingest).** Pass a B2 presigned GET URL for the master as `inputs[].url` on [create asset](https://www.mux.com/docs/api-reference/video/assets/create-asset), with an expiry that covers Mux's download.

Transloadit writes encoding results to B2 through its [Backblaze Store Robot](https://transloadit.com/docs/robots/backblaze-store/); the [Transloadit sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-transloadit-example) gives it a write-only key.

## Security

| Role | Bucket / prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| finishing-writer | `<org>-genvid-delivery` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| transcoder | `<org>-genvid-delivery` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| edge-signer | `<org>-genvid-delivery` / `delivery/` | `readFiles` |
| mux-signer | `<org>-genvid-delivery` / `renders/` | `readFiles` |

The finishing workers also need read access on `published/` in the review bucket. Give them a separate read-only key. Keep the edge signer's key in the CDN's secret store. On takedown, delete the renditions and purge the CDN cache.
